examples.text: Oui, trois cent mille. Je parle de ses vingt ans de carrière.
examples.trans: Yes, three hundred thousand. I'm talking about his twenty years of career.

meanings.note: Soutenir un projet. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to support, to back'.

examples.text: C'est dingue! Tu ne la soutiens pas.
examples.trans: This is crazy! You do not support her.

meanings.note: Sur la table, sur la route. Core French preposition meaning 'on', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Sur haut-parleur = on speaker. Core French preposition meaning 'on', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Le livre est sur la table.
examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: Attention, tu arrives sur la route!
examples.trans: Careful, you're heading for the road!

meanings.note: casual object pronoun, before the verb

examples.text: Je voulais te faire la surprise.
Je ne sais pas. Je voulais te faire la surprise.
examples.trans: I don't know. I wanted to surprise you.

meanings.note: Informal, one owner; ton, ta, tes. Spoken French det expression meaning 'your', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Tes premières vacances en huit ans!
examples.trans: Your first holiday in eight years!

meanings.note: Je ne touche pas à mon visage. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to touch'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'touché').

meanings.en: toucher à: to touch, to tamper with
meanings.note: Je ne touche pas à mon visage. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to touch'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'touché').

examples.text: Je ne touche pas à mon visage.
Désolée, je ne touche pas à mon visage.
examples.trans: Sorry, I'm not touching my face.

meanings.note: toujours aucune nouvelle? = still no news?
Invariable French adverb meaning 'always'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Je suis sérieuse. J'ai toujours adoré le cinéma.
examples.trans: I'm serious. I've always loved films.

meanings.note: takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: trouver quelqu'un sympa = to find someone nice

meanings.en: trouve quelque chose = think of something
meanings.note: In context. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to find'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'trouvé').

examples.text: Je ne sais pas. Trouve quelque chose.
examples.trans: I don't know. Think of something.

meanings.note: one person you know well: friends, family, close colleagues

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi? Mardi, tu as le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday? On Tuesday you've got the Kechiche film.

meanings.note: indefinite article; des in the plural
Number; l'un = one of them. Spoken French det expression meaning 'a', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

meanings.note: + noun or infinitive. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to want'.
Imparfait, softer. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to want'.

examples.trans: I just want to see Mathias.

examples.text: Je voulais te faire la surprise.
Je ne suis pas actrice. Je veux juste voir Mathias.
examples.trans: I'm not an actress. I just want to see Mathias.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Tu crois vraiment qu'il va accepter ce rôle?
examples.trans: Do you really think he is going to accept this role?

examples.text: Je suis vraiment désolée pour ce petit retard.
examples.trans: I am truly sorry for this slight delay.

meanings.note: Il y a = there is / there are. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'there'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
J'y pense = I think about it. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'there'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: S'il vous plaît. Il n'y a rien entre Mathias et moi, d'accord?
examples.trans: Please. There's nothing between Mathias and me, okay?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le yacht', plural 'les yachts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'yacht'.

examples.text: Il invite Juliette sur son yacht privé.
examples.trans: He is inviting Juliette onto his private yacht.

meanings.note: Place: à Paris, à mon cours. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Time: à midi. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

meanings.en: au = à + le, aux = à + les
meanings.note: Contractions. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

meanings.en: écoute = listen, look (to start a point)
meanings.note: Casual imperative. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to listen'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'écouté').

examples.text: Écoute, c'est une industrie, et elle est pleine de requins.
examples.trans: Listen, it's an industry, and it's full of sharks.

examples.text: Il veut écrire, diriger, choisir ses partenaires. C'est l'enfer!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la équipe', plural 'les équipes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'team'.

examples.trans: Yes, I have a great team.

meanings.note: The most common verb. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be'.
Ce + est. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be'.
